import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kummer–Vandiver conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kummer%E2%80%93Vandiver_conjecture)
-/

open NumberField CyclotomicField IsCyclotomicExtension

namespace KummerVandiver

-- TODO(Paul-Lez): change `PNat` to `Nat` once the version of Mathlib we're on allows it.

/--
Kummer–Vandiver conjecture states that for every prime $p$, the class number of the maximal
real subfield of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$ is not divisible by $p$.
--/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem kummer_vandiver (p : ℕ+) (hp : p.Prime) :
    ¬ ↑p ∣ (classNumber (maximalRealSubfield (CyclotomicField p ℚ))) := by
  sorry

end KummerVandiver

reformulations.difference: Mathlib defines maximalRealSubfield using elements real under every complex embedding, whereas the usual maximal real subfield of a cyclotomic field is its intersection with ℝ under a chosen embedding.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For p > 2, the cyclotomic field is CM. Every complex embedding intertwines its canonical conjugation with complex conjugation, so being real under one embedding is equivalent to being fixed by canonical conjugation, hence to membership in maximalRealSubfield. For p = 2, the field is isomorphic to ℚ and is totally real. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved for every permitted p and embedding φ that maximalRealSubfield equals Complex.ofRealHom.fieldRange.comap φ, and proved the corresponding nondivisibility ↔. Class numbers are invariant under field isomorphisms, so using an abstract splitting field also preserves the source's claim.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the cited conjecture, and its research-open category agrees with the source. Lean checks establish that PNat primality quantifies over exactly the natural primes, complex embeddings exist, and the class number is the positive finite cardinality of the ordinary ideal class group. I independently proved that the maximal real subfield at p = 2 has class number 1, so the smallest permitted case is correct. The boundary-case and reformulation proofs compile without sorryAx dependencies. The reviewed file was not modified.
